extracted.intended_audience: Investigators/applicants (and their AORs) seeking to appeal NIAID/NIH peer review decisions, and NIAID program and review staff who process appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Standard operating procedure for filing, evaluating, and processing appeals of peer review for grant applications reviewed at NIH CSR or applicable NIAID NOFOs. Covers permissible grounds for appeal, required documentation, timelines, staff responsibilities, and Council-level decision steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for appeal (flaws in the review process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may appeal the results of peer review only for flaws in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: evidence of reviewer bias; reviewer conflict of interest; lack of appropriate expertise on the committee; factual error that alters the outcome of review. Note: Not all NOFOs allow applicants to appeal (for example, RFAs often do not permit appeals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited grounds for appeal (differences of scientific opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not appeal for differences of scientific opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals based solely on disagreeing with reviewers' scientific judgments will not be considered. Applicants are reminded Council members rarely disagree with the initial peer review outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to discuss concerns with Program Officer before appealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before initiating an appeal, applicants should discuss concerns with their program officer (PO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must have received your summary statement before you initiate an appeal. POs, alone or with SROs, will try to resolve issues as a grievance prior to formal appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized organizational representative (AOR) must submit and sign appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal must be submitted by the applicant's authorized organizational representative (AOR) and the AOR must sign the appeal letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask your AOR to send an appeal letter on your behalf to the PO. The AOR must also sign written requests to withdraw an appeal or to indicate decision to withdraw either appeal or resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for submitting an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals may be submitted from the point of receiving the summary statement until 30 calendar days after the Council meeting (second-level review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's best to submit soon after receiving the summary statement. To be considered for the next Council round, submit before Council meets; preferably at least four weeks before the meeting so POs and SROs have sufficient time to gather information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff attempt resolution before formal appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: NIAID program officers (POs), alone or with scientific review officers (SROs), should try to resolve issues with the applicant as a grievance before initiating the formal appeal process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PO and SRO agree with the request for appeal, the application will be re-reviewed without taking it to Council. If PO or SRO do not agree and concerns cannot be resolved, the appeal process is initiated and referred to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required if PO/SRO do not agree (materials to forward)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the PO or SRO does not agree that an application should be re-reviewed, a set of documents must be forwarded for Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the applicant's written formal appeal; the summary statement; a Special Issue Worksheet summarizing the problem, alternatives, and staff recommendations; and all related correspondence (e.g., emails between PO and SRO), including the SRO rebuttal statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process when PO and SRO agree to re-review (no Council)
rubrics_metrics.description: If PO and SRO agree to re-review, do not take the appeal to Council; instead initiate administrative reassignment for re-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have division coordinators initiate an Assignment Change Request (ACR) indicating the designated SRG and Council date to request a re-review, notify NIAID Receipt and Referral, include correspondence between PO and SRO, and specify whether it should be reviewed in the same SRG or a different SRG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council decision options and downstream steps
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal goes to Council, Council will review staff recommendations and determine whether to approve or deny the applicant's appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council can concur with the SRG and deny the appeal, or support the appeal and recommend the application be re-reviewed by the same or a different SRG. If Council denies the appeal the applicant must accept initial peer review results. If Council approves, NIAID sends Council's recommendation to CSR for final decision on whether to accept or deny the request for re-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Council approval on the application
rubrics_metrics.description: If Council approves the appeal, the original application is re-reviewed; the PI does not revise the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The re-review is conducted by either the same or a different scientific review group (SRG), which does not receive the summary statement or applicant’s appeal letter. NIAID retains original correspondence and provides appeal-related materials to Council for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with resubmission while appeal is unresolved
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant resubmits while an appeal is unresolved, the applicant must choose between the appeal and the resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you learn of a resubmission before an appeal is resolved, contact the investigator to determine whether to appeal or resubmit. If the investigator chooses to resubmit, forward a copy of the written request; the PO will give the investigator five days to withdraw either the appeal or the resubmission. The AOR must sign the request and coordinators will remove the electronic ARA as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO acknowledgement and timeline for responding to an appeal letter
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant sends an appeal letter, the PO must acknowledge receipt in writing within a set timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply to the PI and AOR with an Acknowledgement of Letter of Peer Review Appeal — not an email — within 10 working days. Email a copy of the acknowledgement to the division coordinator, who will initiate an electronic ARA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program division coordinator responsibilities and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Division coordinators must handle administrative steps once an appeal is received or actions are decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate an electronic ARA for the PO and forward the acknowledgement to NIAID Receipt and Referral, the NIAID appeals officer, and NIAID ECB Support. Add the acknowledgement and the ARA to the grant file. If PO and SRO agree to re-review, initiate an ACR, notify Receipt and Referral, post all materials in Council folders, add appeal to pre-Council and Council agendas, and within five days after Council send the Peer Review Appeal Disposition Letter to NIAID ECB Support for signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities in appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: SROs must gather information and participate in resolving appeals and in Council consideration when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify your supervisor upon learning of a potential appeal; gather pertinent information such as the summary statement; work with POs to resolve appeal requests; if not in agreement, write a formal rebuttal statement; attend Council meetings for cases proceeding to Council and prepare to address review questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIAID appeals officer and Council executive secretary roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeals officer provides guidance and oversight of appeal documentation and ensures leadership awareness; the executive secretary handles correspondence and signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Institute director is aware of all appeals before Council; review cases and oversee documentation; forward appeals for Council consideration; provide Council members with appeal letter, Institute recommendation, and any SRO/SRG comments; review and sign the Peer Review Appeal Disposition Letter and send copies to NIAID ECB Support, PO, division coordinator, SRO, and grant file.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIAID ECB Support responsibilities and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: ECB Support reviews appeals materials and ensures appropriate inclusion on Council agendas and appropriate formatting of disposition letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review all appeal letters and associated material, advise staff if materials are missing, ensure appeals are included on pre-Council and Council agendas, review the drafted Peer Review Appeal Disposition Letter for content and format, and forward the final draft of the disposition letter to the NIAID appeals officer within 10 days of Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIAID Receipt and Referral responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt and Referral reviews and approves required administrative forms related to appeals and reassignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and approve ARA and ACR forms and be notified when coordinators initiate or remove electronic ARA/ACR requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and inclusion of appeal materials in the grant file
rubrics_metrics.description: NIAID retains the applicant’s original correspondence and copies of NIH-originated correspondence in the official electronic grant file and provides appeal-related materials to Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division coordinators and staff must add acknowledgement letters, ARA/ACR records, appeal letters, summary statements, Special Issue Worksheets, SRO rebuttals, and other related correspondence to the grant file and appropriate Council folders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory guidance to applicants about appeal likelihood and strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are advised that Council rarely disagrees with initial peer review and most appeals result in a recommendation to revise and resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether revising and resubmitting might be a better option because successful appeals are uncommon and, even if successful, a re-review will occur only at the next cycle. Read 'Should You Appeal?' in Options if Your Application Isn't Funded for additional guidance.
